name: Fanboy
role: His fans' biggest fan — keeps your disks and case cool, just the way you like it
fit.yes: Runs your fans by what actually gets warm — and never forgets his settings
fit.other: {who} runs the fans here — he'd look, say so and steer nothing while it does
fit.no_output: He finds no fan output Linux could steer here — he can read which fan chip the board has and say which driver it needs
fit.no_output_unraid: No fan output yet — the board's fan chip is an {chip}; Unraid's own driver {module} should steer it, and he loads it on your click
fit.no_output_plugin: No fan output yet — the board's fan chip is an {chip}; the plugin {plugin} (by {author}) should bring its driver
fit.no_output_family: No fan output yet — boards of this maker carry ITE chips; the plugin {plugin} (by {author}) should bring their driver
fit.driver_missing: A fan driver plugin is installed, but its driver isn't loaded — he'd show it; the BIOS steers meanwhile
fit.ipmi: This board steers its fans through IPMI — he can't do that yet, but he can send the makers what he sees
greet.1: Listen to them hum — aren't they wonderful?
greet.2: I know every fan by its speed!
greet.3: Phew, is it warm in here, or is it just me?

bubble.ok.one: I found {n} output I could steer. For now the BIOS runs it — set me up and I'll take good care of it!
bubble.ok.other: I found {n} outputs I could steer. For now the BIOS runs them — set me up and I'll take good care of them!

bubble.other: {who} runs the fans here. Only one should steer — so I only watch.
bubble.no_output: I can't find a fan output Linux could steer. I can read which fan chip the board has — then I'll tell you what it needs.
bubble.no_output_unraid: The board's fan chip is an {chip}. Unraid's own driver {module} should take it — shall I load it?
bubble.no_output_plugin: The board's fan chip is an {chip}. The plugin {plugin} should bring its driver — then I can get going!
bubble.no_output_family: Boards like this one carry an {chip} fan chip. The plugin {plugin} should bring its driver — then I can get going!
bubble.driver_missing: A driver plugin for the fan chip is there, but its driver isn't loaded. Until it is, the BIOS steers.
bubble.ipmi: This board steers its fans through IPMI. I can't do that yet.
situation.ok: The BIOS runs every fan. Fanboy only looks until you set him up and let him take over.
situation.other: {who} steers the fans. Only one may steer: Fanboy steers nothing as long as it does. Please switch off the other fan controls first when you want him to take over.
situation.no_output: No fan output Linux could steer was found. Often only a driver is missing.
situation.driver_missing: The driver plugin {plugins} is installed, but its driver ({modules}) isn't loaded — often right after an Unraid update, until the plugin has the driver for the new kernel. The BIOS steers meanwhile.
situation.ipmi: This board steers its fans through IPMI. I can't do that yet. Send us a wish with the report, then we have everything to build it in.
report_tip: Opens the form for a wish with Fanboy's report in it — you see everything before it goes
report_title: Fanboy: what he finds on this board
report_wish: What I'd like Fanboy to do here:
why.other: Fanboy holds back while another plugin steers
outputs.gpu: the graphics card's own — never offered
mode.auto_title: The chip steers this output itself, by its curve (usually the BIOS's)
mode.manual_title: The output stands on a fixed value someone set by hand (the BIOS, a plugin, a script)
mode.full_title: The output runs at full speed, nobody steers it
mode.unknown_title: The chip doesn't say who steers this output
fans.title: Fans and outputs
fans.sub: Each fan connector Linux could steer and what is on it, then every tach input no output of his reads. Click a row for the technical detail.
fans.no_value_title: The input reports nothing right now
sensors.title: Sensors
sensors.sub: Every temperature Linux shows, and Unraid's disks from Unraid's own records — no disk is asked, none is woken.
sensors.asleep_title: The disk sleeps: no temperature while it does (Fanboy never wakes it)
sensors.no_value_title: The sensor reports nothing right now
help.who_text: Who sets the fans' speed now: Fanboy (his zones) or the BIOS — or another plugin —, with the reason; per zone its level and the place that leads it, the fans with their speed. Only the outputs given to him in the setup are his; pumps always stay with the BIOS, and so does the CPU cooler — unless you give it to Fanboy at your own risk. Labels on the outputs: his with the percentage, «watched», «given back». Nothing on this page changes a fan: that is the setup.
help.outputs_text: The chip's fan connectors Linux could steer. «chip steers»: its own curve (the BIOS's); «fixed value»: a value someone set; «full speed»: nobody steers.
help.sensors_text: Every temperature: CPU, NVMe, RAM, board, graphics card — and Unraid's disks as Unraid itself last saw them. A sleeping disk shows no temperature.
help.report_text: Opens the form for a wish with Fanboy's report: the board's model, chips and drivers, how many outputs and inputs, the kinds of sensors, kernel and Unraid version. Never your server's name, serial numbers, disk names or paths.
hints.title: Why is this tricky?
hints.sub: What Fanboy knows about fans, drivers and the BIOS — and what helps. He installs nothing; he loads a driver only on your click.
hints.none_there: None of the plugins Fanboy knows is installed.
hints.st_loaded_title: The plugin is installed and its driver is loaded right now
hints.st_not_loaded_title: The plugin is installed, but its driver isn't loaded — often until the plugin has the driver for a new Unraid
hints.st_steering_title: This plugin steers fans right now — as long as it does, Fanboy steers nothing
hints.st_idle_title: The plugin is installed, but switched off
hints.acpi: Start option for the fan chip
hints.acpi_set_title: acpi_enforce_resources=lax is set at this start
hints.acpi_unset_title: acpi_enforce_resources=lax isn't set — needed only when the BIOS keeps the chip to itself
hints.names_count: {named} named, {hidden} hidden — Fanboy shows the sensors by these names
hints.apps_title: Opens ⟦Apps⟧ — search there for the name and install it yourself
hints.apps_how: In ⟦Apps⟧ search for «{name}» (by {author}) and install it.
hints.board_ite: A hint, not a certainty: {maker} boards mostly carry an ITE chip.
hints.board_nuvoton: A hint, not a certainty: {maker} boards often carry a Nuvoton NCT6687 chip.
plugin.it87-driver: Brings the driver for ITE fan chips (IT86xx, IT87xx), which Unraid lacks for many newer boards.
plugin.nct6687-driver: Brings the driver for the Nuvoton NCT6687 fan chip.
plugin.dynamix.system.temp: Finds the fan chip, loads its driver at every start and lets you name the sensors — but only drivers Unraid brings itself: for a chip only a plugin's driver knows, it can't help.
hints.why_title: Why doesn't Fanboy see my fans?
hints.why.1: The driver for the fan chip isn't part of Unraid. Then a driver plugin brings it.
hints.why.2: Unraid has the driver, but it isn't loaded. Dynamix System Temp finds it («Detect») and loads it at every start.
hints.why.3: The BIOS keeps the chip to itself. Then the driver needs a start option you set yourself: «acpi_enforce_resources=lax» under ⟦Settings⟧ → ⟦Boot Parameters⟧, then restart. Fanboy never sets it.
hints.bios.1: Set each fan connector to its fan's kind: 4-pin fans to PWM, 3-pin fans to voltage (often called «DC» or «Voltage»). Otherwise nobody can steer them — Fanboy neither.
hints.bios.2: A pump stays with the BIOS’s curve, and so does the CPU cooler unless you give it to Fanboy at your own risk. There Fanboy only watches.
hints.clash_title: Who gets in each other's way
hints.clash.1: Dynamix System Autofan, FanCtrl Plus (also FanCtrl Plus 2) and PWM Fan steer the board's fans too. Only one may steer: while one of them runs, Fanboy steers nothing. Please switch off the other fan controls first.
hints.ipmi.1: Some boards steer their fans through IPMI. Fanboy can't do that yet. Send us a wish with his report, then we have everything to build it in.

bubble.steers.one: I steer {n} zone — by what really gets warm. Listen to them!
bubble.steers.other: I steer {n} zones — by what really gets warm. Listen to them!

bubble.alarm: Something's wrong with a fan — I set its zone to 100 % until it's right again.
why.steers: He steers by the warmest spot of each zone
why.chip_missing: The fan chip isn't there — he keeps looking
why.not_armed: Set up, not taken over yet
why.crashed: His control stopped unexpectedly — every fan is handed back
why.released: Given back when the office stopped
why.array_stopped: The array is stopped — the BIOS runs the fans

situation.steers.one: Fanboy steers the fans you gave him, in {n} zone. The CPU cooler, pumps and everything else stay with the BIOS.
situation.steers.other: Fanboy steers the fans you gave him, in {n} zones. The CPU cooler, pumps and everything else stay with the BIOS.

situation.not_armed: Fanboy is set up, but you haven't let him take over yet: the BIOS runs every fan.
out.foreign_title: Someone else changed this output — Fanboy gave it back as it was before him and leaves it alone
out.watched_title: The BIOS steers it — Fanboy does not
notes.title: Lately
note.moved: {fan} was found at another address ({to}) — taken there
note.chip_back: The fan chip is back — Fanboy steers again
note.foreign: Someone else changed {fan} — given back as it was before Fanboy
note.drift: {fan} turns at {rpm} rpm, measured were {want} rpm
note.give_back_failed: {fan} didn't read back as it was before Fanboy
note.alarm_chip: Alarm: the fan chip went away
note.missing_told: {tell_min} minutes without the fan chip — a notification went out
alarm.stands: Alarm: {fan} reports no speed although it should turn. Fanboy sets it and the other fans of its zone to 100 % until it turns again, and then for {min} more minutes.
alarm.bios_stands: Alarm: {fan} reports no speed — the BIOS steers it, Fanboy only watches. Check that fan.
alarm.sensor: Alarm: {source} reports nothing. Fanboy sets the fans of «{zone}» to 100 % until it reports again, and then for {min} more minutes.
alarm.chip: Alarm: the fan chip is gone. Fanboy looks for the chip and takes over when it is back.
control.chip_missing: Fanboy doesn't steer: the fan chip isn't there — often its driver is missing after an Unraid update. The BIOS runs the fans; he keeps looking and takes over when it comes.
control.crashed: Fanboy’s control stopped unexpectedly. Every fan is handed back (to the mainboard’s automatic or to the value from before, as «When giving back» says). The messenger starts it again, unless that happens several times in a short while.
control.look_now_tip: Fanboy looks for the fan chip right now
drivers.title: Load the driver yourself
drivers.text: Fanboy can try the fan-chip drivers Unraid brings itself, one after the other. Nothing is downloaded, nothing is written to the flash; what helps he loads again at every start.
drivers.self: You can also do it yourself: in ⟦Apps⟧ install the plugin Dynamix System Temp — it finds and loads the driver as well, from the same drivers Unraid brings.
drivers.r.no_output: {module}: loaded, but no output he could steer — unloaded again
drivers.r.no_chip: {module}: no chip of its kind here
drivers.r.acpi: {module}: the BIOS keeps the chip to itself
drivers.acpi: The kernel says the BIOS keeps the fan chip to itself. Fanboy changes nothing about that — the third reason under «Why doesn't Fanboy see my fans?» says what helps.
drivers.none: No driver of the list found a fan chip here.
drivers.none_next: None of Unraid's own drivers found a fan chip here. The next step is the plugin «{plugin}» (by {author}): search for it in ⟦Apps⟧ and install it.
drivers.load: Look for drivers and load them
drivers.load_tip: Tries the fan-chip drivers Unraid brings, one after the other — only on this click
drivers.undo_tip: Unloads the drivers Fanboy loaded here and forgets them
drivers.none_toast: No driver found a fan chip
chip.title: Your fan chip
chip.not_read: Fanboy can ask the fan chip for its name, directly at the mainboard's configuration port — the way Linux's own drivers and sensors-detect do it. Only on this click, never by itself; nothing on the chip is changed.
chip.read_tip: Asks the board's fan chip for its name — only on this click, nothing is changed
chip.not_read_toast: The fan chip couldn't be read
chip.blocked.no_port: Fanboy can't ask the fan chip here: this Unraid gives no access to the chip's ports.
chip.blocked.locked: Fanboy can't ask the fan chip here: the kernel is locked down and keeps the chip's ports closed.
chip.blocked.held: Fanboy doesn't ask the fan chip now: the driver {modules} is loaded and talks to it.
chip.blocked.no_open: Fanboy couldn't open the chip's ports — nothing was asked.
chip.blocked.io: Asking the fan chip broke off — Fanboy stopped and left it as it was.
chip.blocked.maker: Fanboy never asks the fan chip on a Gigabyte board: such boards carry ITE chips, often two, and Linux's own ITE driver warns that touching them from outside can upset the board. What helps is known anyway: the plugin «{plugin}» (by {author}) should bring the driver for ITE chips — once it is loaded, Fanboy names the exact chip.
chip.blocked.no_maker: Fanboy doesn't ask the fan chip here: the board doesn't say who made it, and on some boards (Gigabyte's) such a question can upset the board. The words below and the report still help.
chip.found: The fan chip answered: {chip} (id {id} at port {port}).
chip.need.unraid: Unraid's own driver {module} should steer it — «Look for drivers and load them» tries it.
chip.need.plugin: Unraid's own drivers don't know this chip. The plugin «{plugin}» (by {author}) should bring its driver.
chip.need.plugin_read: Unraid's own driver {module} only reads this chip — temperatures and speeds, nothing to steer. The plugin «{plugin}» (by {author}) should steer it.
chip.need.newer: Unraid's own driver {module} knows this chip from kernel {since} on — a newer Unraid should steer it.
chip.need.read_only: Its driver {module} shows temperatures and fan speeds only: no driver is known that steers this chip.
chip.need.unknown: The fan chip answered with id {id} at port {port} — a chip Fanboy doesn't know yet.
chip.need.nothing: No fan chip answered at the two usual ports. Then the fans are run elsewhere: by the BIOS through a controller Linux can't reach, by a USB or AIO controller (its driver loads by itself when Unraid sees it), or through IPMI.
chip.need.held: Not read: the driver {modules} is loaded, but it shows no output either. The hints below say why that happens — often the BIOS keeps the chip to itself.
chip.plugin_how: In ⟦Apps⟧ search for «{plugin}» (by {author}) and install it.
chip.plugin_after: Its notes ask for no restart: it loads its driver right away, and Fanboy sees the outputs at his next look.
chip.plugin_restart: The driver nct6683 is loaded now and holds the chip: after installing, a restart of Unraid may be needed before the new driver gets it.
chip.words_hint: To look it up yourself (from the board's maker — a hint, not a certainty):
chip.words_where: The plugin by its exact name in ⟦Apps⟧; the chip and the board together with «fan» in the Unraid forum.
chip.words_where_forum: The chip and the board together with «fan» in the Unraid forum.
chip.report_text: So Fanboy can learn it: send the chip's id and the board's name — nothing else of your server.
chip.report_tip: Opens the form for a wish with the chip's id, the board's name and the Unraid version — you see everything before it goes
chip.report_title: Fanboy: a fan chip to learn
chip.report_wish: Please teach Fanboy this fan chip:
chip.to_hints_tip: Opens «Setup» at its first step: what fits here, the drivers, why it's tricky
errors.fanboy_busy: Fanboy is busy with his settings — try again in a moment.
errors.fanboy_step_running: A setup step is running — wait until it is done or stop it.
errors.fanboy_steering: Fanboy steers right now — hand the fans back first.
errors.fanboy_other: {who} steers the fans. Only one may steer — please switch off the other fan controls first.
errors.fanboy_not_his: That fan stays with the BIOS (CPU cooler, pump, «don't know» or no feedback) — Fanboy never tests it downward.
errors.fanboy_bad_role: That isn't a role Fanboy knows.
errors.fanboy_bad_name: The name is too long ({max} characters at most).
errors.fanboy_bad_place: That isn't a place Fanboy knows.
errors.fanboy_off_needs_measure: «Off» needs a measured fan with feedback — measure it first.
errors.fanboy_bad_zones: The zones don't fit what is there ({field}).
errors.fanboy_rpm_needs_measure: Steering by rpm needs every fan of the zone measured, with feedback.
errors.fanboy_no_zones: No zone with a fan of his yet — set up the zones first.
errors.fanboy_no_modprobe: Loading a driver isn't possible here.
errors.fanboy_drivers_there: Fanboy sees fan outputs already — no driver to load.
errors.fanboy_chip_io: Asking the fan chip broke off — Fanboy stopped and left it as it was.
notify.alarm_stands: {fan} ({zone}) reports no speed although it should turn. Fanboy sets it and the other fans of its zone to 100 % until it turns again, and then for {min} more minutes.
notify.alarm_bios_stands: {fan} reports no speed — the BIOS steers it, Fanboy only watches. Check that fan now.
notify.alarm_sensor: {source} («{zone}») reports nothing. Fanboy sets the fans of «{zone}» to 100 % until it reports again, and then for {min} more minutes.
notify.alarm_chip_subject: Fanboy: the fan chip went away
notify.alarm_chip: The fan chip went away while Fanboy steered. Nobody steers now: the fans stay at the values he wrote last. Fanboy looks for the chip and takes over when it is back. If it gets warm: at a restart of Unraid most mainboards set their fans anew — Fanboy has not checked this on your board.
notify.foreign: Someone else changed {fan} behind Fanboy's back — no plugin Fanboy knows: a script or a container? He gave it back as set for this output (its state before him or the mainboard's automatic) and leaves it alone.
notify.drift: {fan} turns at {rpm} rpm where its measurement says {want} rpm — replugged or replaced? Measure it again on Fanboy's page.
notify.missing: The fan chip hasn't been there for {min} minutes — often its driver is missing after an Unraid update. The BIOS runs the fans; Fanboy keeps looking.
notify.back: The fan chip is back — Fanboy steers the fans again.
notify.net_warm_subject: Fanboy: {source} is warm and in no zone
notify.net_warm: {source} is at {c} °C and no zone of yours has it. Fanboy runs every fan he steers at least at {pct} % until it has cooled down — put it into a zone so its fans react to it.
notify.net_hot_subject: Fanboy: {source} too warm — in no zone
notify.net_hot: {source} is at {c} °C, too warm for a heat source none of your zones has. Fanboy runs every fan he steers at 100 %.
notify.crashed: Fanboy's control stopped unexpectedly. Every fan it held is given back as set for it (its state before him or the mainboard's automatic). He starts it again by himself after {pause} s — after {max} stops within {window} minutes no more.
check.fanboy_steers: Fanboy steers the fans he took over
check.fanboy_steers_how: Open Fanboy's page: it says why he doesn't (the fan chip missing, another plugin steering, his control stopped) and what helps.
check.fanboy_alarm: No alarm at Fanboy's fans: every fan turns, every sensor answers
check.fanboy_alarm_how: Open Fanboy's page: it says which fan or sensor. A fan of his standing, too warm at full or a silent sensor: the fans of that zone are at 100 % until {min} minutes after the reason ended. A fan the BIOS steers standing: Fanboy only watches it.
bubble.ready: All set up — say «Take over» and they're mine. I can hardly wait!
bubble.testing: Listen! I'm turning one output after the other up — every fan gets its moment. «Stop everything» brings every fan back at once.
bubble.measuring: Slowly down, step by step — I want to know exactly how low each one can go.
bubble.chip_missing: The fan chip isn't there. The BIOS runs the fans; I keep looking.
bubble.array_stopped: The array is stopped. The BIOS runs the fans until it starts again.
out.name: Output {n}
out.untested_title: The setup hasn't tested this output yet — it belongs to the BIOS
out.empty_title: Nothing turned when the setup tested it: the connector is empty, it stays with the BIOS
out.no_role_title: A fan was found here — say in the setup what it is
out.his_title: One of the fans you gave Fanboy — the BIOS runs it until you let him take over
fans.sub_steers: Each fan connector Linux could steer: his with the percentage he sets, the BIOS's watched. Click a row for the technical detail.
fans.input_title: A speed input no output of his reads — often the CPU cooler on its own connector, or an empty one
server.sub: Your fans and what they cool, as a picture. Each wheel turns roughly as fast as its fan.
server.sub_steers: His zones as pieces of the case: the fans turn about as fast as they really do, the air goes from the front through to the back, the warmest spot of each zone is framed. Sleeping disks are only marked — he never wakes them.
pic.watched_title: The BIOS steers it — Fanboy does not
pic.asleep_title: The disk sleeps: no temperature while it does — Fanboy never wakes it
pic.warmest_mark: the warmest spot of this zone
pic.all_note: Before the setup: every fan that turns, run by the BIOS
pic.all_note_none: Before the setup: without a driver for the fan chip, Linux shows no fan here
pic.bios_zone_note: CPU cooler and pumps — Fanboy only watches them
curves.title: History
curves.sub: Per zone the chosen period: the temperature of the place that led (line) and the speed he gave (shaded). Point at a chart to read a moment in every zone.
curves.none: No zone yet — the setup makes them.
curves.line_bios: The BIOS runs this zone's fans right now.
curves.history_label: The history ({period}): the warmest spot and the speed
curves.history_none: No history yet — it fills a point a minute while he steers.
curves.key_curve_tip: {kind}: the warmest place of this curve, its highest value in each 5 minutes
hints.st_other_fans_title: It steers shelf and IPMI fans, not the board's outputs — Fanboy steers beside it
hints.waz: WAZ Cooling Control steers the fans of disk shelves and IPMI chassis, not the board's fan connectors: Fanboy steers beside it. Should it ever change one of his outputs, he notices, gives that output back as it was before him and leaves it alone.
hints.clash.2: WAZ Cooling Control steers disk shelves and IPMI fans, not the board's connectors — Fanboy steers beside it.
control.array_stopped: The array is stopped: the BIOS runs every fan. Fanboy takes over again when it starts.
step.detect_sub: What the mainboard shows: the outputs Linux could steer, and how each stands now. This step only reads.
step.test_sub: One output after the other: it runs at 100 % until you say whether you heard it — then every fan runs as before again. Then you enter what it is and «Save and go on» starts the next. Without an answer the test pauses after {hold_min} minutes ({hold_quiet_min} while the other fans stand).
step.measure_sub: Only his fans with speed feedback: step by step from full down to its lowest steady speed and its start value. Too warm or stopped: everything goes back at once. Measuring usually takes about {measure_usual_min} minutes per fan, at most {measure_min}. Let it run through.
step.zones_sub: A zone is fans plus what they cool plus a curve. Move fans and heat sources between zones, choose quiet, normal or cool, or drag your own curve. Saved here, steering only after «Take over».
step.take_sub: Now he steers the fans you gave him. «Hand back» gives each one back at once: to the mainboard’s automatic or to the value from before, as «When giving back» says.
step.stop_tip: Stops the step now — every output goes back as it was
step.stopped_toast: Stopped — the outputs are going back
step.ended.stopped: The last step was stopped. Every output it held went back as it was.
step.ended.page_gone: The last step stopped because the page was closed or reloaded. Every output it held went back as it was.

step.ended.unanswered.one: Paused: no answer for a minute, so every output went back as it was. The next output was not started.
step.ended.unanswered.other: Paused: no answer for {n} minutes, so every output went back as it was. The next output was not started.

save.next_tip: Saves what you entered for this output in one go, then starts the test of {fan}
save.tip: Saves what you entered for this output in one go
save.role_first: First say what it is — then it can be saved.
strip.next_waits: {fan} starts as soon as the last test has ended and every fan runs as before

test.resume_tip.one: Tests the output still open — each again until you answer
test.resume_tip.other: Tests the {n} outputs still open, one after the other — each until you answer

step.ended.interrupted: The last step was interrupted (the office restarted). Every output it held went back as it was.
step.ended.warm: The last step stopped because something got too warm. Every output went back as it was — try again when it has cooled down.
step.ended.too_long: The last step took too long and stopped. Every output went back as it was.
step.ended.error: The last step failed. Every output went back as it was; the office's log says more.
detect.mode.auto: The chip steers it itself (its curve) · now {pct} %
detect.mode.unknown: The chip doesn't say who steers it · now {pct} %
detect.fixed: A fixed value something else set ({pct} %)

detect.fixed_note.one: {n} output stands on a fixed value something else set. In «Test and assign» (its output, «When giving back») you choose what «give back» means for it.
detect.fixed_note.other: {n} outputs stand on a fixed value something else set. In «Test and assign» (each output, «When giving back») you choose what «give back» means for them.

test.one_tip: Turns this output up to full until you answer — then exactly back as it was
test.all_tip: One output after the other at full, each until you answer — then back as it was
test.again_tip: Turns it up again so you can listen
test.unclear: It ran at full speed already — up shows nothing
test.yes_tip: A fan without speed feedback is on it
test.no_tip: The connector is empty: it stays with the BIOS and leaves the list
test.busy: Someone else holds this output right now
roles.cpu_hint: A hint, not a certainty: output 1 is often the CPU cooler.
roles.bios_note.cpu: The CPU cooler stays with the BIOS: Fanboy only watches that it turns.
roles.bios_note.unknown: When in doubt it stays with the BIOS — Fanboy does not steer it.
back.title: Give back to
back.text: Before Fanboy this output stood on a fixed value something else set ({pct} %). When he stops or you hand back, it goes to:
measure.none: No fan of his with speed feedback — nothing to measure. Fans without feedback get a safe lowest speed.
measure.one_tip: From full speed down step by step — then back exactly as it was
measure.all_tip: Each of his fans with feedback in turn, from full speed down — then back as it was
measure.done: Lowest steady {min} % · start value {start} % · up to {max} rpm
measure.no_turn: It didn't turn at full speed — check it; Fanboy leaves it as it is
measure.warm: Stopped: too warm — measure again when it has cooled down
zones.no_fans: No fan of his yet — give fans a role under «Test and assign» first.
zones.propose_tip: Zones from the roles: the disk cage's fans with every disk, the rest with NVMe, RAM and the board
zones.empty: No zone yet — take his proposal or add one.
zones.unzoned: Not in any zone yet (the BIOS keeps them): {list}
zones.name: The zone's name
zones.remove_tip: Removes the zone from the page — its fans go back to no zone
zones.off_ok_tip: Off: below its lowest speed this fan may stop completely. Default: no — it never stands
zones.no_fan: No fan in this zone yet.
zones.sources_sub: Click to take one in or out. The warmest counts; a sleeping disk counts as asleep, never as cold. Depending on the drivers installed, some sensors may appear more than once or be missing.
zones.sources_first: No heat source yet — choose at least one; until then the zone's curve does nothing.
zones.curve_sub: Drag a point or type its values below.
curve.locked: Quiet, Normal and Cool are fixed. To move points, choose «Own curve» — it starts from the curve you see here.
curve.locked_kept: Quiet, Normal and Cool are fixed. «Own curve» brings back your last own curve for it.
curve.under_quiet: Your curve is only at {pct} % at {c} °C — «Quiet» would be at 100 % there.
curve.never_off_all: No fan of this zone may stand: where the curve says 0 %, they turn at their minimum ({list}).
curve.never_off_one: This fan may not stand: where the curve says 0 %, it turns at its minimum ({list}).
curve.never_off_some: Where the curve says 0 %, only {stand} stands. Never off despite 0 %: {keep}.
zones.unit_tip: Every fan of the zone is measured: he can steer by rpm
zones.unit_off: rpm only when every fan of the zone is measured with feedback
zones.save_tip: Keeps the zones as shown — if Fanboy steers, he takes them over at once
zones.undo_tip: Back to the zones as saved
dry.run_tip: Shows what he would set now — writes nothing
dry.not_found: Not every fan was found right now ({why}).
dry.nothing: Nothing warm right now — the quiet level
dry.nothing_written: Nothing was written — that only happens after «Take over».
take.text: He takes over the fans of his zones and steers them by what really gets warm. The CPU cooler, pumps and everything else stay with the BIOS.
take.go_tip: Fanboy steers the fans of his zones from now on

take.confirm.one: He steers {n} zone from now on. «Hand back» gives every fan back at once: to the mainboard’s automatic or to the value from before, as «When giving back» says.
take.confirm.other: He steers {n} zones from now on. «Hand back» gives every fan back at once: to the mainboard’s automatic or to the value from before, as «When giving back» says.

take.no_zones: No zone with a fan of his yet.
take.step_runs: A setup step is running — wait until it is done.
take.armed: Taken over — he is about to steer.
take.hand_back_tip: Every fan back at once, as «When giving back» says for it
take.hand_back_text: «Hand back» gives every output back at once: to the mainboard’s automatic or to the value from before, as «When giving back» says.
take.hand_back_confirm: Every fan he steers goes back now: to the mainboard’s automatic or to the value from before, as «When giving back» says. His setup stays — you can let him take over again any time.
take.given_back: He has given every fan back: to the mainboard’s automatic or to the value from before, as «When giving back» says.
sensors.in_zone: A heat source of this zone
help.picture_text: Each zone as a piece of the case: its fans in the walls where the air comes in and goes out, the heat sources between them. A wheel turns about as fast as its fan; red: it stands although it should turn; dashed: no speed feedback; «BIOS»: the BIOS runs it. Reduced motion in your system: still wheels with an arc for the speed.
help.curves_text: Per zone the chosen period: the temperature of the place that led (a line) and the speed he gave (shaded). Point at a chart, tap it or move with the arrow keys: a line marks the moment in every zone's chart, and above each chart stand its time, the level, the fans' speed and which place led with its temperature («warmest spot» for moments recorded before he kept its name). A curve's shape is set in the setup, step «Zones».
help.setup_text: Five steps, one after the other: detect, test and assign, measure, zones, take over. Each tile opens its step alone; the whole page shows all of them, and under them the settings (his Dashboard tile, the fans he only watches). Every step is built alike: on top the strip that says what runs right now (with «Stop everything»), left the list, right the field for the row you chose, at the bottom what is still open and the one button that leads on. Why fans are tricky, drivers and the BIOS: under the first step.
help.safe_text: Until «Take over» nothing changes for good: tests and measuring give every output back exactly as it was — also when the page closes (after 45 seconds) or the office stops.
help.later_text: A curve, a zone, a fan's model: open its step alone and change it — the rest stays. Tests and measuring again need the fans handed back first.
errors.fanboy_bad_back: That isn't a choice Fanboy knows.
errors.fanboy_no_auto: This chip has no automatic for that output.
back.no_auto_note: This chip has no automatic mode for the output: it goes back to the fixed value ({pct} %).
back.default_note: Unless you choose otherwise: the mainboard's automatic.
fans.group_bios_sub: a fan on it, or not tested yet
fans.none_first: No output with a fan on it.

fans.more.one: {n} more: empty outputs and bare speed inputs
fans.more.other: {n} more: empty outputs and bare speed inputs

sensors.too_warm_title: Over Unraid's warning for this disk, or the sensor the alarm names
sensors.group_zone: heat sources of this zone, the warmest first
sensors.none_first: No sensor of a zone fits — the others are below.
dash.why.not_armed: set up, not taken over yet
dash.why.starting: Fanboy is about to take over
dash.why.released: given back when the office stopped
dash.stale: As of {when} — his page brings new numbers
dash.span_tip: Change the span — next: last {next} h
dash.curve_none: No curve yet — Fanboy records one while he steers.
dash.setting_sub: A tile of his own on Unraid's Dashboard — move or hide it there like any other. For everyone who opens the Dashboard.
dash.show.off_title: No tile of his on the Dashboard
dash.show.speeds_title: Who steers; each zone's warmest spot and level, and its fans with their speed
dash.show.history_title: The speeds, and a small curve of the last hours for each zone
errors.fanboy_bad_period: That isn't a period Fanboy keeps.
step.nothing: Nothing to set up here — the note above says why.
step.blocked_other: Only once nothing else steers the fans.
pic.on_one_title: {n} fans on one connector — one speed for all of them
hints.hub.1: With a Y-cable or a hub several fans hang on one connector: Fanboy sets them all to the same value and sees only one speed — usually the first fan's.
hints.hub.2: So the slowest of them can stand without him noticing. Say in the setup how many hang on it, and look at them now and then.
roles.count_note: {n} fans share this connector: one value, one speed reading for all of them.
errors.fanboy_bad_count: Between 1 and {max} fans on one connector.
step.blocked_steering: Only once you have handed the fans back (step 5).
step.ended.warm_what: Measuring stopped: {where} was at {c} °C — Fanboy's threshold for measuring is {below} °C. Every output went back as it was — try again when it has cooled down.
alarm.stands_alone: Alarm: {fan} reports no speed although it should turn. Fanboy sets it to 100 % until it turns again, and then for {min} more minutes.
notify.alarm_stands_alone: {fan} ({zone}) reports no speed although it should turn. Fanboy sets it to 100 % until it turns again, and then for {min} more minutes.
zones.how_often: Fanboy looks every {s} seconds. The disks' temperatures are as fresh as Unraid polls them itself — he only reads Unraid's record.
react.title: How he reacts
react.profile: {up} · down: {gap} °C under the highest, after {hold} s, about {step} % every {s} s
react.profile_now: {up} · down: {gap} °C under the highest, about {step} % every {s} s
cpu.risk_1: Fanboy steers it only while Unraid and the office run. If his control stops, the guard gives the cooler back to the mainboard’s automatic; if it does not turn afterwards, it is set to 100 %.
cpu.risk_2: If the whole server hangs, nobody gives it back: it stays at its last speed.
cpu.risk_3: The CPU then protects itself: it slows down or switches off. Nothing breaks, but the server gets slow or goes off.
cpu.risk_4: Only recommended when the BIOS’s curve is not good enough. Fanboy never keeps it under {floor} % while it runs, and stops it only if you allow that yourself («may stand still»).
cpu.confirm: I have read this and let Fanboy steer the CPU cooler at my own risk.
cpu.go: Fanboy steers it from now on
cpu.go_tip: Stores your confirmation with the date; then the CPU cooler goes into a zone with the CPU temperature.
cpu.own_since: CPU cooler: steered by Fanboy, at your own risk since {date}.
cpu.back_tip: The BIOS steers it again; Fanboy only watches that it turns.
cpu.no_auto: Fanboy can't take it over here: this output has no mainboard automatic he could give it back to.
errors.fanboy_cpu_confirm: Tick the box first: Fanboy steers the CPU cooler only with your confirmation.
errors.fanboy_cpu_no_auto: This output has no mainboard automatic — the CPU cooler stays with the BIOS.
errors.fanboy_cpu_zone_needs_cpu: A zone with the CPU cooler needs a CPU temperature as a heat source.

situation.steers_cpu.one: Fanboy steers the fans you gave him, in {n} zone — the CPU cooler too, at your risk. Pumps and everything else stay with the BIOS.
situation.steers_cpu.other: Fanboy steers the fans you gave him, in {n} zones — the CPU cooler too, at your risk. Pumps and everything else stay with the BIOS.

take.text_cpu: He takes over the fans of his zones and steers them by what really gets warm — the CPU cooler too, at your risk. Pumps and everything else stay with the BIOS.
why.chip_gone: The fan chip went away — the fans stay as Fanboy set them last
bubble.chip_gone: My fan chip is gone! Nobody steers now — the fans go on as I set them last. I'm looking for it.
control.chip_gone: Nobody steers: the fan chip went away while Fanboy steered. The fans stay at the values he wrote last — neither he nor the BIOS changes them. He looks for the chip and takes over when it is back. If it gets warm: after a restart of Unraid the BIOS usually steers the fans again. If the driver is missing after an update, look at the driver plugin.
notify.missing_stuck_subject: Fanboy: the fan chip is still missing
notify.missing_stuck: The fan chip has been missing for {min} minutes — often its driver is missing after an Unraid update: look at the driver plugin. Fanboy keeps looking.
pic.nobody_now: nobody steers them now — they stay as they were
curves.line_nobody: Nobody steers this zone's fans now — they stay as Fanboy set them last.
pic.stuck_title: Nobody steers this fan — it stays as Fanboy set it last
test.ignored: Doesn't obey — the BIOS keeps this connector
test.ignored_hint: Fanboy never steers it. To give it to him: choose a fixed or flat setting for this connector in the BIOS and test again — otherwise it stays with the BIOS.
test.inverted: The other way round: more power makes it slower
test.inverted_hint: The driver steers this connector the other way round. Fanboy gave it back at once and never steers it; it stays with the BIOS.
out.ignored_title: The BIOS keeps this connector — Fanboy never steers it
out.inverted_title: More power makes this fan slower — Fanboy never steers it, it stays with the BIOS
notify.not_back_subject: Fanboy: the mainboard didn't take {fan} back
notify.not_back: After Fanboy gave it back, {fan} turned clearly slower than before — the mainboard didn't take it back. Fanboy set it to 100 %; it stays so until Fanboy steers it again. At a restart of Unraid most mainboards set their fans anew — Fanboy has not checked this on your board.
notify.refuses_subject: Fanboy: the driver takes no values for {fan}
notify.refuses: The fan chip's driver refuses every value for {fan}. Fanboy gave it back as set for this output, as far as the driver still takes it, and doesn't steer it any more. A restart may help; otherwise send Fanboy's report to the makers.
note.refuses: The driver takes no values for {fan} — back to the BIOS
hints.poll: Unraid reads the disks' temperatures again only every {min} minutes
hints.poll_how: A disk temperature Fanboy sees can be that old. Make it shorter under ⟦Disk Settings⟧ at «poll_attributes» (in seconds). Fanboy never changes it.
zones.poll: Here Unraid renews them only every {min} minutes (see the hints).
situation.vm: Unraid runs in a virtual machine here: the fans belong to the host.
situation.twins: Two drivers sit on the fan chip {chips} at once (e.g. nct6683 and nct6687) — it doesn't take values reliably so. Fanboy doesn't steer it until only one is loaded.
hints.twins: Two drivers on one chip: {chips} — Fanboy leaves it alone
notify.idle_stands_subject: Fanboy: {fan} stands while it is warm
notify.idle_stands: {fan} has reported no speed for {min} minutes although {source} is at {c} °C. Fanboy doesn't steer this fan, he only watches it. Check it — his page shows which fans stop only while everything is cool.
watch.setting_sub: Fanboy tells you when a fan he doesn't steer stands while something is warm — before any setup too. A fan that stops only while everything is cool (the BIOS's «fan stop») he just notes. He never writes to these fans.
watch.on_title: A fan he doesn't steer that stands while something is warm: a notification after {idle_min} minutes
watch.off_title: Fanboy watches only the fans he steers and the CPU cooler and pump while he steers
watch.stops_cool_title: It stood while everything was cool — the BIOS's «fan stop» or another controller's 0 %. Fanboy notes it and tells nothing; standing while something is warm he tells.
watch.stands_warm_title: It stands although {source} is at {c} °C. Still standing after {idle_min} minutes: Fanboy tells you.
watch.alarm_title: It stands although something is warm; Fanboy sent a notification. Over when it turns again.
watch.banner: {fan} stands although {source} is at {c} °C. Fanboy doesn't steer this fan, he only watches — check it.
watch.banner_cool: {fan} stood while something was warm and hasn't turned since. Fanboy doesn't steer this fan, he only watches — check it.
show.tip: Only this fan to 100 % for up to {show_s} seconds, then back exactly as it was — listen and look which one speeds up
show.toast: {fan} runs at 100 % for up to {show_s} seconds — then back as it was
show.off.ignored: This output does not obey (the BIOS keeps it) — Fanboy never steers it and cannot show it
show.off.inverted: This output works the other way round — Fanboy never writes it
show.off.other: Another fan control steers — switch it off first
show.off.step: A setup step is running — afterwards
show.off.one: Another fan is being shown — one at a time
show.off.alarm: An alarm is on — show it once the alarm is over
show.give_back_failed: After showing {fan}, its output didn't read back as it was before — look at it in the fans list; after a restart of Unraid the BIOS usually steers it again.
errors.fanboy_show_running: A fan is being shown right now — one at a time.
errors.fanboy_show_alarm: An alarm is on. Show it once the alarm is over.
errors.fanboy_show_not: This output does not obey, works the other way round, or its driver takes no values — Fanboy never steers it and cannot show it.
hints.poll_add: Values up to {min} minutes old — I add {add} °C to them in my zones (such a value is a lower bound of the truth).
zones.poll_add: So Fanboy adds {add} °C to each disk value.
show.stop_tip: Ends the show now: the fan goes back exactly to what it was
help.show_text: Only while Fanboy steers — testing then waits until you have handed the fans back (step 5) — a fan already found can be shown: only this one goes to full speed for up to a minute, every other fan keeps running exactly as it is. Afterwards it goes back to its curve (a fan of the BIOS: to exactly what it was). «Found it — stop» ends it earlier. Before he steers, «Test again» does the same.
help.flow: Test and assign, output by output
help.flow_text: One output after the other: «Test this output» turns it to 100 % — with «stop the other fans meanwhile» every other fan stands for that time, the CPU cooler and a pump too. «Found it — done» or «Heard nothing — done» ends the test and every fan runs as before. Then you enter what it is, its name, where it sits, how many hang on it and, if you like, its look — saved only with «Save and go on», which tests the next output at once. A finished output can be opened and saved again.
help.places_text: Front, rear, top, bottom, side — or «On the CPU» (a CPU cooler's fan) and «Inside the case» (a pump, a fan on the RAM or an NVMe). What fits its role is offered first. The place counts only for the picture «The server»: a fan on the CPU or inside the case stands there among the heat sources.
help.chip_text: When Linux shows no fan connector, «Your fan chip» says which chip sits on the mainboard (read on your click, never on a Gigabyte board), which driver or driver plugin it needs (for ITE or Nuvoton chips, say) and the words to search for.
help.dash_text: Under «Settings», «Show on the Dashboard»: off, the speeds, or the speeds with their history. Once your fans have a look or a name, the tile shows each with its symbol, its name and its speed; a fan standing on purpose says so.
why.fixed: The outputs stand on a fixed value someone left
bubble.fixed: Nobody steers here right now: the fans stand on a fixed value someone left. After a restart of Unraid the BIOS usually steers them again — or set me up!
situation.fixed: Nobody steers: {list} stand on a fixed value someone left (an uninstalled fan plugin, for example). After a restart of Unraid the BIOS usually steers them again — or set Fanboy up.
situation.fixed_some: {list} stand on a fixed value someone left — nobody steers them. After a restart of Unraid the BIOS usually steers them again.
take.fixed_before: {list} stood on a fixed value someone left before Fanboy — not with the BIOS. Hand back, and they go back to that fixed value; the BIOS usually steers them again only after a restart of Unraid. Best restart Unraid first and let Fanboy take over afterwards.
take.fixed_before_auto: {list} stood on a fixed value someone left before Fanboy — not with the BIOS. Hand back, and they go to the mainboard's automatic (as «When giving back» says). Safest: restart Unraid first and let Fanboy take over afterwards.
pic.fixed_title: Nobody steers this fan — its output stands on a fixed value someone left
pic.all_note_fixed: Before the setup: every fan that turns — nobody steers them (a fixed value someone left)
server.sub_fixed: Your fans and what they cool, as a picture. Every wheel turns about as fast as its fan; right now nobody steers them — they stand on a fixed value.
quiet.setting: Stop the other fans meanwhile (easier to hear)
quiet.on_title: While one output is tested, every other one is set to 0 % — only that fan is heard
quiet.off_title: The other fans run on as they are — no other output is written
step.ended.quiet_warm: The test stopped: {what} was at {c} °C with the other fans standing. Every output went back as it was — try again when it has cooled down, or with «stop the other fans» off.
step.ended.no_restart: The test stopped: {what} didn't turn again after the other fans stood. Fanboy set its output to full speed and sent a notification — look at that fan.
show.quiet_warm: Showing stopped early: {what} was at {c} °C with the other fans standing. Every fan is back as it was.
show.no_restart: {what} didn't turn again after the other fans stood. Fanboy set its output to full speed and sent a notification — look at that fan.
help.quiet_text: The one exception to «never down»: while one output is tested (until you answer, three minutes at most), every other fan is set to 0 % so only that one is heard — the CPU cooler and a pump too. Not every board or fan stops completely; some keep their lowest speed. He doesn't start while anything is warm and brings everything back at once when the CPU rises or a place gets warm; afterwards every fan must turn again, or its output goes to full and you get a notification. Off: no other fan is touched.
errors.fanboy_quiet_warm: Not with the other fans stopped right now: {what} is at {c} °C. Try again when it has cooled down, or with «stop the other fans» off.
notify.quiet_no_restart: {fan} turned before the test with the other fans stopped and didn't turn again afterwards. Fanboy set its output to full speed and stopped the test — check that fan.
test.found_next_tip: You know which fan it is: this output goes back as it was, after a short pause the next one
test.abort_tip: Ends the whole test now — every output back as it was
assign.never_stopped: From now on it is never stopped while other outputs are tested.
role.left: Don't test — leave it with the BIOS
test.left: Not tested — stays with the BIOS
safety.no_restart: Fanboy set it to 100 % for safety — it didn't start again by itself after it stood (before: {pct} %).
safety.not_back: Fanboy set it to 100 % for safety — the mainboard didn't take it back after he gave it back (before: {pct} %).
safety.back_tip: Back to {pct} % as before — if it doesn't start by itself, it gets a short kick
safety.back_all: All back to the value before
safety.back_tip_all: Each back to its value before — a fan that doesn't start by itself gets a short kick
safety.wait: Only once nothing else runs (a test, a show)
safety.banner: Fanboy set {list} to 100 % for safety — it didn't start again by itself after it stood. Back to the value before: here, or at its output in the setup.
assign.kick: Needs a kick to start: it keeps turning at {pct} %, but doesn't start from standing there.
busy_wait: One moment — the last click is still on its way.
stop_all_tip: Ends a test or show at once and puts every output back to its state before — a fan that doesn't start by itself gets a short kick
bubble.showing: There it goes — that's the one! «Stop everything» brings every fan back at once.
bubble.safety: I set a fan to 100 % for safety — it didn't start by itself. «Back to the value before» puts it back.
assign.cpu_bios: CPU cooler — steered by the BIOS; never stopped while other outputs are tested.
errors.fanboy_cpu_role_first: First give the fan the role «CPU cooler», then choose who steers it.
errors.fanboy_hub_one: This looks at a connector with several fans on it — say first how many hang on it.
errors.fanboy_uncovered: Some heat sources are in no zone while fans may stand still: {sources}. Take over anyway only if you mean it.
errors.fanboy_cpu_off_confirm: Letting the CPU cooler stand needs its own tick: you confirm the CPU then cools without a fan whenever it is cool.
errors.fanboy_cpu_off_bios: The BIOS steers this CPU cooler — Fanboy never stops it.
errors.fanboy_off_not_safe: Measure this fan again first: only one whose measuring found that it stops and starts again safely may stand.
strip.idle: Nothing of the setup is running right now. Every output is as it was before.
strip.test_quiet: Running now: {fan} at 100 % — the other fans stand still meanwhile.
strip.test: Running now: {fan} at 100 % — the others go on as before.
strip.show_quiet: Running now: {fan} at 100 %, so you can find it — the other fans stand still meanwhile.
strip.show: Running now: {fan} at 100 %, so you can find it — the others go on as before.
strip.measure: Being measured now: {fan} — its output stands at {pct} %.
strip.pause: Pause: the fans are starting again — {s} s to go.
strip.pause_next: Pause: the fans are starting again — {s} s to go, then {fan}.
strip.pause_plain: Pause: the fans are starting again.

strip.safety.one: {list} runs at 100 % for safety. Nothing else of the setup is running.
strip.safety.other: {list} run at 100 % for safety. Nothing else of the setup is running.

strip.keep_open: Keep this page open. If it closes, this ends after {lease_s} seconds and every output goes back.
warm.tick: Start anyway — I know {where} is already at {c} °C.
warm.tick_none: Start anyway — I know Fanboy can't read the CPU's temperature.
warm.note: Counts for the next start only. Fanboy then doesn't stop that run because of warmth: the fans being tested may stand or run slowly for a moment while it is this warm — keep an eye on it yourself. If the page closes, everything still goes back after {lease_s} seconds.
warm.note_none: Counts for the next start only. Fanboy then lets the CPU cooler stand for its test even without the CPU's temperature — keep an eye on it yourself. If the page closes, everything still goes back after {lease_s} seconds.
strip.warm_off: Running without the warmth guard (your tick) — keep an eye on the temperatures yourself.
strip.away: The messenger isn't here right now — this works again once he is back.
quiet.hint_1: Not every mainboard stops a fan completely — some fans then go on quietly.
quiet.hint_2: Switched on, every other fan stands while one is tested — the CPU cooler and a pump too.
quiet.hint_3: If anything gets warm, Fanboy stops the test and all fans run again at once.
quiet.off_note: The other fans go on as before — Fanboy writes to no other output.
list.label: The mainboard's outputs
label.now_tip: This output is at 100 % right now
label.stands_tip: Stopped by Fanboy while the other output runs — afterwards as it was before
label.waits_tip: Its turn comes later in this test
label.empty_tip: No fan hangs here: the output stays with the BIOS
label.ask_tip: No fan input followed — say whether a fan hangs here
label.what_tip: A fan was found — say what it is
label.left_tip: Not tested: this output stays with the BIOS
label.untested_tip: This output has not been tested yet
label.bios_tip: Stays with the BIOS — Fanboy does not steer it
panel.now: Running at 100 % now, and it stays so until you answer. Go and hear which fan gets loud — and say below what it is.
panel.showing: Running at 100 % now, so you can find it.
panel.stands: stands still while the other one runs
panel.safety: Runs at 100 % — Fanboy set it so for safety.
panel.busy: {fan} is running right now. Testing works afterwards — you can already fill in things here.
panel.to_run_tip: Shows the output that runs now — where you answer whether you heard it
panel.pause: A short pause, the fans are starting again. You can already fill in things here.
panel.empty_note: Nothing hangs here: the output stays with the BIOS. A fan on it after all? Then test it again.
panel.role_first: Where it sits and how many there are comes once you have said what it is.
test.none_tip: You hear no fan: if no fan input follows either, the connector counts as empty and stays with the BIOS
what.title: What is it?
what.empty_tip: Nothing hangs on this connector: it stays with the BIOS
what.tip.cpu: The CPU cooler stays with the BIOS — unless you give it to Fanboy at your own risk
what.tip.pump: A pump always stays with the BIOS
what.tip.unknown: When in doubt it stays with the BIOS
fields.name: What do you call it?
look.text: Only for the picture. The model is a proposal — colours and blades are yours to set. Its speeds come from Fanboy’s measuring.
next.open_ask: Does a fan hang here? Say it
panel.queued: Its turn comes in this test. You can already fill in things here.
strip.kick: A push: a fan didn't start by itself and gets full power for a moment — {s} s to go.
strip.restore: {fan} is going back to its value from before.
strip.waits_left: waits for your answer · pauses in {time}
label.measuring_tip: Fanboy is measuring this fan right now, step by step from 100 % downwards
measure.table_none: No table yet. Measuring fills it: what percent gives which speed, the lowest steady value and the start value.
panel.queued_measure: Its turn comes in this run.
panel.busy_measure: {fan} is being measured right now — this works afterwards.
zones.incomplete_tip: A zone needs at least one fan and one heat source
take.his_tip: Fanboy steers this zone's fans once you let him take over
take.bios_tip: Fanboy does not steer these — they stay with the BIOS
strip.steers: Fanboy is steering right now. Testing and measuring work again once you have handed the fans back (step 5).
strip.other: Another fan control is steering. Testing and measuring work once nothing else steers.
panel.kept: Noted. It is saved together with what the fan is — say that above.
strip.ending: Ending — the output is going back …
strip.stopping: Stopping — every output is going back …
zones.stand_never: never stands — the BIOS steers it
zones.stand_silent: never stands — it has no speed feedback
zones.stand_measure: may stand still: measure it first
zones.stand_unsafe: never stands — it doesn't start again safely
zones.cpu_stand_title: Let the CPU cooler stand still?
zones.cpu_stand_go: Yes, it may stand — at my own risk
zones.preset_pct: Quiet, normal and cool exist only in percent — set «In» to percent first.
strip.m.stop_check: Checking the standstill: {fan} is at 0 % — does it stop?
strip.m.stop_check_s: Checking the standstill: {fan} is at 0 % — does it stop? {s} s to go.
strip.m.start_find: Looking for the start value: {fan} — now {pct} %.
strip.m.kick: Start with a push: {fan} gets full power for a moment, then {pct} %.
measure.p.stop_check: The standstill is being checked — the output is at 0 %
measure.p.start_find: Looking for the value it starts from standing — now {pct} %
measure.p.kick: It gets a push (full power for a moment), then {pct} %
stand.starts: Stands still at 0 % · starts again from {pct} %.
stand.kick: Stands still at 0 % · starts again only with a push (then {pct} %).
stand.floor: Never stands quite still: at 0 % it goes on at {rpm} rpm.
stand.unsafe: Doesn't start again safely after standing — it may never stand still.
stand.unknown: The standstill hasn't been tried yet — measure it again and it can be allowed to stand.
stand.cut_rise: Standstill not passed: {where} rose from {from} to {c} °C while it stood — it always keeps turning.
stand.cut_at: Standstill not passed: {where} was at {c} °C while it stood — Fanboy's threshold for measuring is {below} °C. It always keeps turning.
stand.cut_none: Standstill not passed: the CPU reported no temperature while it stood — it always keeps turning.
step.ended.no_cpu: Stopped: the CPU reports no temperature — without it Fanboy never lets the CPU cooler stand. Every output went back as it was.
zones.stand_again: may stand still: measure it again first
zones.stand_floor: never stands — at 0 % it goes on at {rpm} rpm
off_why.measure_again: not in effect: measure it again so it may stand
off_why.never_stops: not in effect: it never stands quite still
off_why.not_safe: not in effect: it doesn't start again safely
off_why.not_measured: not in effect: measure it first
off_why.cpu_off_confirm: not in effect: your confirmation is missing
curve.says_stand: Stands still up to {t} °C. Above that it runs with at least {floor} %.
curve.says_floor: Never runs under {floor} % — also where the curve asks for less.
curve.says_cpu: It stops again at the earliest after {cool} seconds under {below} °C; a single reading of {hard} °C or more starts it at once.
cpustand.what: It may stop completely while the CPU is cool — the CPU then has to do without a fan.
curve.says_never_zero: The curve asks for 0 % nowhere — so it never stands, and it runs with at least {floor} %.
cpustand.curve: By your curve it stands while the CPU is under {start} °C. It starts again from {start} °C — at once on a single reading of {hard} °C or more — and stops again at the earliest after {cool} seconds under {below} °C.
cpustand.never_zero: Your curve asks for 0 % nowhere — so it will never stand until you draw the curve down to 0 % at the bottom.
cpustand.gone_seen: If Fanboy fails, the output goes back to the mainboard's automatic (seen to take over on this mainboard on {date}).
cpustand.gone_unseen: If Fanboy fails, the output is set back to the mainboard's automatic; whether your mainboard's automatic then takes over has not been checked yet.
cpustand.hang: If the whole server hangs, nobody sets it back.
off_why.curve_never_zero: not in effect: its curve asks for 0 % nowhere
dry.title: This is what I would set right now
look.proposal_tip: Colours and blades as this model usually comes. Change what is different on yours.
look.changed_tip: At least one of these is your own choice, not the model’s proposal.
look.reset_tip: Sets frame, blades, their shape and number and «reverse blade» to the model’s proposal again.
look.undo_tip: Puts back the model and your own choices from before.
look.reverse_tip: A reverse-blade fan has inverted blades: it blows the other way through its frame and turns as usual. Every picture of this fan shows its blades mirrored. Only for the picture — the control doesn’t change.
look.reverse_model: This model is a reverse-blade fan as made.
look.gallery_tip: Every fan of the list drawn, by maker — see them all, then choose one with a click.
zones.uncovered: These heat sources are in no zone: {list}. No fan follows them — only when one of them gets too warm does Fanboy let the fans he steers run faster.
zones.uncovered_in_tip: Adds the heat source to the zone shown here. Kept only with «Save the zones».
take.uncovered_confirm: In no zone: {sources}. Allowed to stand: {fans}. While these fans stand, no fan follows these heat sources — only when one of them gets too warm does Fanboy let the fans he steers run faster. Take over like this?
net.on: A heat source outside the zones is warm: {source} {c} °C — every fan Fanboy steers runs at {level} % or more.
note.net: Outside the zones, {source} was warm at {c} °C — the fans ran faster
note.net_over: {source} is cool again — the fans follow their zones again
curve.says_stand_all: This curve asks for nothing up to {t} °C. He stands only while no kind of the zone asks for anything — otherwise he runs at {floor} % or more.
curve.says_never_zero_kind: The curve for {kind} asks for 0 % nowhere — while one of those heat sources is awake he does not stand. He runs at {floor} % or more.
curve.says_cpu_else: The CPU cooler stands only by the CPU’s curve. For this kind he runs at {floor} % or more.
curve.leads_tip: Of all heat sources in this zone, one of this kind asks for the most right now — the fans follow it.
curve.kind_tip: Show the curve for {kind} in front
zones.curve_no_source: Give the zone a heat source first — then its curve shows here.
why.alarm_watch: Alarm: a fan the BIOS steers stands
bubble.alarm_watch: A fan the BIOS steers stands — I can only watch that one. Please have a look.
src_group.unassigned_tip: Disks outside the array and the pools, as Unraid lists them. Disks on a controller passed to a VM as a whole Unraid does not see — Fanboy cannot take those as heat sources.
src.in_use_title: This disk is being read or written, but Unraid shows no temperature for it. In a zone it counts like a sensor that says nothing: after a while the zone goes to 100 % with an alarm.
help.vm_disks_text: Disks outside the array and the pools show as «Unassigned / used by VMs» and can be heat sources of a zone. Disks on a controller passed to a VM as a whole Unraid does not see — Fanboy cannot take those as heat sources.
hub.alike: The same fans on every plug?
hub.alike_yes_tip: The same model on every plug: what was measured counts for all of them
hub.alike_no_tip: Different fans: Fanboy keeps them a little higher, so that none stalls
hub.alike_unknown_tip: Not sure: Fanboy treats them as different fans
hub.title: {n} fans on this connector
hub.table: The table counts for the fan that reports its speed.
hub.same: The same fans on every plug: what was measured counts for all of them.
hub.mixed: Several different fans: Fanboy keeps them a little higher (minimum {floor} %, start {start} %).
hub.unchecked: Whether all of them start again has not been checked with your eyes yet — until then he may not stand still.
hub.ok: Checked with your eyes: all of them start again.
hub.not_safe: Not all of them start again — he may never stand still.
hub.look_tip: Fanboy sets this connector to its minimum, stops it, starts it again — and asks you each time whether all fans do it
hub.look_silent: The look needs a fan that reports its speed on this connector.
hub.look_bios: The BIOS steers this connector — nothing for Fanboy to check here.
hub.ask.hub_stop: All of them stand … in a moment they start again.
hub.ask.hub_start: Do all of them start again at {pct} %?
hub.ask.pause: Fanboy checks that every fan turns again …
hub.yes_tip: Every fan on this connector does it
hub.no_tip: At least one fan does not
hub.result.ok: All of them turn and start again.
hub.result.floor_up: Not all of them turned — the minimum is {floor} % now. Check once more.
hub.result.not_safe: Not all of them started again — he may never stand still.
hub.result.no_answer: No answer within a minute — nothing was changed.
hub.result.warm: Stopped: it got too warm. Everything is back.
strip.h.hub_turn: {fan} runs at {pct} % — do all fans turn? Answer at its panel.
strip.h.hub_stop: {fan} stands — in a moment it starts again.
strip.h.hub_start: {fan} starts at {pct} % — do all fans start again? Answer at its panel.
zones.stand_hub: may stand still: first check with your eyes whether all fans on it start again (step 3)
zones.stand_hub_no: may stand still: no — not all fans on it start again
off_why.mixed_hub: not in effect yet: first check with your eyes whether all fans start again
off_why.hub_not_safe: not in effect: not all fans start again
panel.busy_hub: Right now {fan} is being checked with your eyes — this works afterwards.
bubble.hub_look: Look closely: I ask you whether every fan on this connector does it. «Stop everything» puts every fan back at once.
zones.hub_same_tip: The same model on every plug of this connector: what was measured counts for all of them, and he may stand like any measured fan
zones.hub_look_tip: Opens step 3 at this fan: there Fanboy shows you whether all fans on the connector start again
control.crashed_n: Fanboy’s control stopped unexpectedly. Every fan is handed back (to the mainboard’s automatic or to the value from before, as «When giving back» says). The messenger starts it again after {pause} s — not any more after {max} stops within {window} minutes.
control.crashed_given_up: Fanboy’s control stopped unexpectedly {max} times within {window} minutes — the messenger no longer starts it by itself. Every fan is handed back (to the mainboard’s automatic or to the value from before, as «When giving back» says). Let Fanboy take over again once you know why, or send his report to the developers.
zones.uncovered_pct: These heat sources are in no zone: {list}. No fan follows them — only when one of them gets too warm does Fanboy let the fans he steers run at {pct} % or more.
now.title: Now
now.not_set_up: Fanboy isn't set up yet — the BIOS steers every fan.
now.not_armed: Fanboy is set up, but you haven't let him take over yet — the BIOS steers every fan.
now.bios: Right now the BIOS steers every fan.
settings.title: Settings
settings.sub: For the whole office, not just this browser: his tile on Unraid's Dashboard and the fans he only watches.
hist.read_hint: Point at a chart (or tap it) to read a moment — in every zone at once; arrow keys move the marker.
